title: Sev2: coordinated response for GPU OOMs, KV-cache corruption, and memory fragmentation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Morales
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported elevated GPU OOMs and unexplained memory growth on hosted and dedicated clusters over the last 36 hours. Parallel alerts surfaced on private deployments indicating KV cache corruption and increased allocator fragmentation leading to degraded throughput. This ticket is the engineering response coordinating triage, short-term mitigations, a runtime patch, and customer comms.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC: First signed alert (hosted-prod-us-east) of recurring GPU OOM during long-context streaming.
- 2026-03-10 01:00 UTC: Dedicated customer (AcmeHealth) paged support for spike in tail-latency and eventual OOM on a pinned pool.
- 2026-03-10 04:20 UTC: Private deployment (BetaCorp VPC) reported KV-cache checksum mismatches after node eviction.
- 2026-03-10 08:00 UTC: SRE stabilized impacted pools with forced restarts and config changes (reduced batch_size, disabled prefix caching for affected routes).

Investigation notes and partial decisions:
- Root cause hypothesis currently: a confluence of (1) a regression in LRU eviction introducing stale KV entries that cause unexpected allocations when the runtime deserializes large key ranges; (2) allocator behavior on CUDA drivers that, under high churn, produces fragmentation and delayed reuse resulting in spike OOMs for long sequences.
- Repro steps identified in internal lab against a reproducer harness: long-context workloads (>= 4096 tokens) + high-concurrency (>= 48 concurrent streams) + prefix cache turned on = deterministic memory growth in ~2 minutes. Repro script: scripts/repro/gpu_oom_kv_leak.sh (linked in attachments).
- Evidence for corruption: dumped cache checksums differ across nodes after live migration; KV entry header counters show non-monotonic increases.

Short-term mitigations applied (already deployed to hosted and dedicated):
1) Disable prefix caching by default for requests with sequence_length > 2048 and concurrency > 24 (config change rolled at 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC).
2) Enforce soft OOM guard for each worker that triggers token-stepped backoff and drains KV jobs before restart.
3) Pin a conservative allocator policy on affected instance types to reduce fragmentation (driver-level knob).
These mitigations reduced customer error rates by ~78% in the first 6 hours (monitoring: dashboard runtime-ooms/reduction-2026-03-10).

Planned runtime patch (target: runtime-1.24.1, hotfix channel):
- Fix A: KV cache eviction race: add a lightweight epoch-based guard around eviction + checksum validation on rehydrate to prevent use-after-free semantics for cache entries. (PR: runtime#2738)
- Fix B: Allocator cooperative compaction: introduce a periodic compaction window for CUDA-backed allocators triggered when fragmentation metric > 0.35. Compaction runs are bounded (max 200ms) and staggered to avoid synchronized stalls. (PR: runtime#2742)
- Fix C: Defensive deserialization: validate header lengths and checksum before allocating large buffers; fall back to streaming deserialize path on mismatch.

Testing and rollout plan: 
- Stage rollout in three waves: CI -> canary cluster (hosted-canary) -> reserved dedicated pools -> private repo package for customers.
- Tests: reproduce script in CI; fuzzed KV sequences; integration perf harness measuring latency and throughput with compaction enabled.
- Canary target: 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours; monitor error budget and memory metrics.
- Rollback: feature flag for compaction and KV guard to disable with immediate effect. Backout plan documented in runtime/deploy/backouts.md.

Customer communications and follow-ups: 
- Outbound: support drafted customer advisory with timeline, impact, and temporary mitigations (sent to impacted customers 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC).
- Next steps for major customers: coordinate private-package with BetaCorp and AcmeHealth for in-place upgrade window (contact leads: pm@beta.redwood, se@acmehealth).

Observability & long-term work items (postmortem actions):
- ENG-9089: Add KV cache invariant metrics (per-shard checksum drift, stale-hit counters).
- ENG-9096: Expand allocator telemetry (historic free-span histograms, fragmentation index).
- ENG-9102: E2E chaos tests for node eviction and live migration to validate cache rehydration paths.
- Console: create per-customer memory-health alert templates and a one-click mitigation to toggle prefix-cache.

Open risks and blockers: 
- Driver compatibility: compaction relies on CUDA 12.2 helpers; some private customers on pinned 11.x stacks will need staged installers. Blocker referenced in dependencies.
- Repro environment parity: some customer runs include custom kernels; reproducer needs to be validated on those configs.

Current action items (owner / status):
- Marcus Nguyen: land PR#2738 (eviction guard) and pair with QA for deterministic repro tests (In Progress).
- Leila Park: implement compaction telemetry hooks and create dashboards (In Progress).
- SRE (Jorge Rivera): schedule canary rollout and update runbook for soft OOM guard (Planned).
- PM (Nina Kapoor): coordinate customer upgrade windows and update advisory (In Progress).

Notes and links: PRs and test artifacts are in pr_urls and attachments. For quick triage run: ./scripts/triage/oom-kv-triage.sh --cluster hosted-canary --since 2026-03-09.

Acceptance criteria for Done: 
- Hotfix merged and deployed to hosted canary with metrics showing >90% reduction in OOM rate for the reproducer within 48h.
- Dedicated pools receiving the patch show stability for 7 days with no recurring KV checksum drift incidents.
- Private customers have validated the package or received a safe backout and signed off.
- Postmortem published with timeline, root cause, and the ENG-90xx follow-ups scheduled.
